items.title: David Spinozza interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, NY, September 27, 2025
items.q: I got most of how I play jazz from listening to horn players. Like I would listen to Lee Morgan for instance like that

ctx.x: So where did you access in your head how to write for horns? Was there something you heard growing up that you were paying attention to?

Well I always listened – I used to listen to – it was funny, even some of my guitar lines come from horn players. I got most of how I play jazz from listening to horn players. Like I would listen to Lee Morgan for instance like that, I had that record “Sidewinder” you know. And I’d arranged that a few times for my band. But I was studying music theory in high school. I had a really good music theory teacher. So he would teach me how to take dictation, how to write stuff out, and so I was learning how to do that…
If you’re writing for just two, did you discover like what’s the most effective thing of the notes in the chord – if it’s just two horns.
